audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer credits Karma's root to Mantra-Q in three places: content early "she roots me with Mantra-Q (RQ)" and "her RQ tether", spikes[0].text "Mantra-empowered Q (RQ) poke and tether", wants.foe[0] "Mantra-Q (RQ) root-tether".
audit.why: Inner Flame and its Mantra version have no root at all — Mantra-Q adds a delayed cataclysm of damage. The root is Focused Resolve, the W: a tether that roots if it is not broken, with Mantra-W extending the root and healing her. The full layer of this same matchup has it right, so the two layers currently teach opposite things. A player watching for a root on her Q will walk into the real one every time.
audit.corrected: Named Focused Resolve (W) as the root in early, spikes[0].text and wants.foe[0].
sources: champ-data/_kits/karma.json (W Focused Resolve: tether, root, hardCC flag; Q Inner Flame Mantra bonus: "creating a cataclysm which deals damage after a short delay")

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere says that eating her poke has a cost beyond the HP.
audit.why: Gathering Fire reduces Mantra's cooldown every time one of her damaging abilities lands. Mantra is 40/38/36/34s on paper, but against a melee who has to keep stepping into the wave it is far shorter than that in practice. That reframes the whole lane: every chip she lands is buying her the next empowered ability, so dodging matters even at full health.
audit.corrected: Added Gathering Fire to breakdown.mid and content mid.
sources: champ-data/_kits/karma.json (P Gathering Fire: "Karma's damaging abilities will reduce the cooldown of Mantra"; R Mantra cd 40/38/36/34)

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry tells the player to eat poke he "cannot punish" without giving him the one tool that actually reduces it.
audit.why: Inner Flame explodes on the first enemy unit it hits, so a minion between Nasus and Karma absorbs the poke outright. For a champion whose entire early game is standing in the wave last-hitting, where he stands relative to the minion line is the only lever he has.
audit.corrected: Added the detonate-on-first-unit rule to content early.
sources: champ-data/_kits/karma.json (Q Inner Flame: "a ball of spirit energy that explodes and deals damage upon hitting an enemy unit", range 950)

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry treats level 6 as a normal ult-vs-ult stage.
audit.why: Mantra is available at level 1 and costs no skill point. Karma has no level-6 spike at all, which is both why her early game is so heavy and why level 6 is a genuine one-sided swing for Nasus rather than a mutual power stage.
audit.corrected: Stated it in tldr and content mid.
sources: champ-data/_kits/karma.json (R Mantra: "available at level 1 and does not require a skill point")

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names Focused Resolve as matchup-defining but gives it no number, and content whys[5] says she pokes "from outside Wither range" without either range.
audit.why: Focused Resolve is 12s flat at every rank — it never gets shorter, so the window after a used tether is the same all game. Inner Flame reaches 950 and Wither reaches 700, which is the exact 250-unit gap the player is being told to live inside.
audit.corrected: Put 12s into breakdown.cooldowns and breakdown.mid, and the 950-vs-700 gap into whys[5] and wants.foe[0].
sources: champ-data/_kits/karma.json (W cd 12 at all ranks; Q range 950)

audit.whatIsWrong: full tldr opens "He denies your stacks from range" — Karma is referred to as "she" everywhere else in the entry.
audit.why: Straight pronoun error in the first line the player reads.

edits.before: He denies your stacks from range — take Fleet + Doran's Shield, farm what's safe, and out-scale. Nasus wins by trading around Karma's Focused Resolve and cashing the pattern: stack, survive, and out-scale — Wither wins the rematch.
edits.after: She denies your stacks from range — take Fleet + Doran's Shield, farm what's safe, and out-scale. Mantra needs no skill point and is up from level 1, which is why her early is this heavy: stack, survive, and let Wither win the rematch.

edits.before: - Karma Focused Resolve: matchup-defining — Her root tether — breaks if you LoS / outrange it. Track it before every engage.
edits.after: - Karma Focused Resolve: matchup-defining — her root tether, 12s flat at every rank. Break it by distance or eat the root.

edits.before: Trade strictly around Focused Resolve: when it is down, run your full pattern; when it is up, give nothing. If ahead, freeze and starve her.
edits.after: Trade around Focused Resolve's flat 12s, and remember Gathering Fire refunds Mantra off every ability she lands, so eating poke is never free.

edits.before: Karma owns the entire early game, so do not pretend otherwise — I have no ult, barely any stacks, and Spirit Fire (E) is my only ranged tool, while she roots me with Mantra-Q (RQ) and pokes my fat HP bar from outside my reach. I just last-hit with Siphoning Strike (Q) and farm stacks under tower, eating the poke I cannot punish. Do not flat-out walk at her to trade — her RQ tether plus E shield mean I take three pokes for every auto I land, and Wither isn't up until level 3 anyway. Soak the lane, deny nothing, and survive.
edits.after: Karma owns the entire early game, so do not pretend otherwise — I have no ult, barely any stacks, and Spirit Fire (E) is my only ranged tool, while she roots me with Focused Resolve (W) and pokes my fat HP bar from outside my reach. I last-hit with Siphoning Strike (Q) and farm stacks under tower, eating the poke I cannot punish. Inner Flame (Q) explodes on the first unit it touches, so hold the minion line and it lands on a caster instead of me. Do not walk at her to trade — her tether plus E shield mean three pokes for every auto I land.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay hers — she's shoving with empowered Q waves or poking me down while I hoard stacks and play not to die. Wither (W) at 3 lets me peel a gank or punish a wild overstep, but I don't own any window here; her E shield and RE move speed bail her out of any half-commit I make. Level 6 is my one even swing: Fury of the Sands plus a Wither on a target who stepped up turns a single all-in in my favor, since the ult's bonus HP and per-second magic damage plus my lifesteal can grind her down if she's in melee. Bait out her E shield and RE dash, THEN W and run her down — don't burn Wither while she still has the move speed to ignore it.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay hers — she's shoving with empowered Q waves or poking me down while I hoard stacks and play not to die. Every ability she lands refunds Mantra through Gathering Fire, so the poke I eat is buying her next empowered cast. Wither (W) at 3 lets me peel a gank or punish a wild overstep, but I don't own any window here; her E shield and RE move speed bail her out of any half-commit I make. Level 6 is my one even swing, and it changes nothing for her since Mantra never needed a point: Fury of the Sands plus a Wither on someone who stepped up turns a single all-in my way, the ult's bonus HP and magic damage plus my lifesteal grinding her down in melee. Bait the E shield and RE dash, THEN W.

edits.before: Karma's Mantra-empowered Q (RQ) poke and tether shreds you off the wave before you have Wither or stacks to answer.
edits.after: Karma's Focused Resolve (W) root plus Inner Flame poke shreds you off the wave before you have Wither or stacks to answer.

edits.before: Poke you off your stacks with Mantra-Q (RQ) root-tether and chip your fat HP bar from outside Wither range
edits.after: Root you off your stacks with Focused Resolve (W) and chip your HP bar from 950, outside Wither's 700

edits.before: Her first item (Liandry's/Lich Bane plus E shield and RE move speed) lets her kite and poke you down from outside Wither range — her threat peak.
edits.after: Her first item (Liandry's/Lich Bane plus E shield and RE move speed) lets her kite and poke from 950 while Wither only reaches 700 — her threat peak.

notes: suspectNames flagged "Soak Siphoning Strike" in wants.you[0] — false positive, Siphoning Strike is the correct Q name and the extra token is the verb. The checker missed the real error in the same matchup, which was the root being attributed to Mantra-Q instead of Focused Resolve. breakdown.cooldowns claims the tether "breaks if you LoS / outrange it"; the kit confirms a tether that can be broken, but says nothing about line of sight breaking it, so I wrote only "break it by distance" and left the LoS claim out rather than repeat something I could not verify. Level chart untouched: content win[] gives Karma 5 of 7 stages against a 51.92% Nasus win rate over 1273 games, which looks tilted, but every stage label matches its own why text and the win rate is plainly earned in the last stage rather than in lane — I would rather leave it than invent a mid-lane power shift.
